title: Squared length decomposition
statement: Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a Boolean function, let $g_1,\ldots,g_m:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $x\in\{0,1\}^n$. If $V(f,g)(x)=(D_1f(x),\ldots,D_nf(x),g_1(x),\ldots,g_m(x))$, where $D_i$ is the coordinate half-difference, then $\sum_{j=1}^{n+m}V(f,g)(x)_j^2=\sum_{i=1}^n(D_if(x))^2+\sum_{j=1}^m g_j(x)^2$.
hypotheses_covered: $g$ is a family of $m$ real-valued functions on $\{0,1\}^n$
replaced: For $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and $g=(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$ of real functions on the cube, write $V(f,g)(x)=(D_1f(x),\ldots,D_nf(x),g_1(x),\ldots,g_m(x))$ and $F_P(f,g)=\mathbb E\sqrt{P(f)^2+\|V(f,g)\|_2^2}$, with $D_i$ the coordinate half-difference. For every $x$, $\|V(f,g)(x)\|_2^2=\sum_i(D_i f(x))^2+\sum_jg_j(x)^2$.
